sections.html:
• Common names: Manila sea catfish, Kanduli
  • Synonym: Pseudarius philippinus

Philippines: in coastal waters, estuaries, and freshwater. Type locality: Manille.

Arius manillensis is a species of marine catfish endemic to the island of Luzon, Philippines. It is found in the area around Manila, Bataan, Laguna, Cavite, and Rizal, including the Pasig River and Laguna de Bay.
It inhabits marine, brackish, freshwater, and benthopelagic habitats.

Arius manillensis are mouthbrooders. The males incubate the eggs within their mouths for six to eight weeks and provide shelter for the young once they hatch. A single instance of a female carrying eggs in her mouth has also been reported.

Upon hatching, the young forage for plankton in short bursts but will quickly return to the safety of the mouth of the adult if alarmed. They eventually become independent once they reach a size of 30 to 44 mm. During the entire period, the adults do not eat and their stomachs shrink dramatically.

Etymology: the specific name manillensis refers to the area around Manila, the Philippines. It was first described by the French zoologist Achille Valenciennes in 1840.

IUCN Red List: This species is widely distributed and exploited commercially in Luzon, Philippines. Information on the current population status is not directly available. Aggregated fisheries data for catfishes overall suggest a 17.3% reduction in all catfish populations over the past 10 years, and this decline is projected to continue due to overexploitation and destructive fishing methods. The species may potentially qualify for a threatened category, but due to insufficient species-specific information it is assessed as Data Deficient. The subpopulation in Laguna Province has declined by 82% from 2011-2020 based on fisheries production data, and conservation of this species in Laguna Province should be a priority (IUCN 2022).
